title: The Board Assembler
briefing: Motherboards as dicts were fine for testing, but the assembler needs proper blueprints. A class is a blueprint, and every board built from it is an object with its own data and its own abilities. Design the Motherboard blueprint, then a fancier GamingBoard that inherits from it, and the Motherboard floor is complete!
hints: __init__(self, ...) runs when a board is created. Store things on the object with self.serial = serial. Every method's first parameter is self.

install_ram should raise ValueError when len(self.ram) is already equal to self.ram_slots, otherwise append. __str__ must RETURN a string. class GamingBoard(Motherboard): inherits, and super().__init__(serial, socket, ram_slots=8) runs the parent's setup.

class Motherboard: def __init__(self, serial, socket, ram_slots=4): self.serial = serial; self.socket = socket; self.ram_slots = ram_slots; self.ram = [] / def install_ram(self, stick): if len(self.ram) >= self.ram_slots: raise ValueError("No free RAM slots"); self.ram.append(stick) / def __str__(self): return f"Motherboard {self.serial} ({self.socket})" / class GamingBoard(Motherboard): def __init__(self, serial, socket): super().__init__(serial, socket, ram_slots=8); self.rgb = True
bonus: Add a class attribute boards_built = 0 to Motherboard and add 1 to it (Motherboard.boards_built += 1) inside __init__. Build 3 boards and print the count.
